task: Malformed form bodies are only logged today. parse_body_arguments and parse_multipart_form_data write a warning to gen_log and carry on, so one bad request can spam the log and the handler still runs with partial arguments. Make them raise HTTPInputError instead, once per request, and make a tornado.web application answer such a request with a 400 without running the handler method. parse_multipart_form_data must raise HTTPInputError for: no final boundary, a part with no header block ("multipart/form-data missing headers"), a disposition other than form-data or a part that does not end in CRLF ("Invalid multipart/form-data"), and a part with no name ("multipart/form-data missing name"). parse_body_arguments must raise HTTPInputError for: a Content-Encoding header on a urlencoded or multipart body ("Unsupported Content-Encoding: <encoding>"), an undecodable urlencoded body ("Invalid x-www-form-urlencoded body: <error>"), a multipart content type with no boundary, and any other multipart failure ("Invalid multipart/form-data: <error>"). On the web side the error must pass through the normal RequestHandler error path, as an HTTPError with status 400, so write_error and log_exception run and the log line carries the parse message. For example a gzip-encoded form POST to a server without decompress_request must return 400 and log a gen_log warning that matches the regex .*Unsupported Content-Encoding. Handlers using @stream_request_body do not get their body parsed and must not change.
